name: Lord of the Asylum: Christmas Chaos

date.source: The fed's own pay-per-view billing page and the results page's own header: "Christmas Chaos 12.31.02 ... Live from Atlanta, GA ... 8/7 Central, Only On PPV!!" (/promotions/dwo/archive/loa-christmas-chaos-billing-2002.html).

matches.note: Chryste, under a mask as Serpente, and a cloaked companion attacked both wrestlers after the finish; she unmasked in the ring.
A preliminary round of the fed's own DWO World Championship tournament.

notes: The fed's own year-end pay-per-view, and the night Chryste returned under the mask of Serpente. Its two halves were served on two pages; this is the first, and its own final matches and double main event continue on the second (/promotions/dwo/archive/loa-christmas-chaos-2002-12-31-continued.html). The World Title tournament ran across it: Kaiowas beat Vash and Julius Corbin beat Shawna Blaze to make the final, which the fed booked for the following Travesty.

name: Lord of the Asylum: Christmas Chaos, continued

date.source: The second half of the same night; the fed served it on its own page under the title "Christmas Chaos Continued".

matches.note: A semi-final of the fed's own DWO World Championship tournament, with a shot at the World Title on the line.

For ownership of the DWO. Callisto Bane pinned her wife to take the company back; a figure then dropped from the rafters, hanged Draven on a steel cable and hit Callisto twice with a sledgehammer, and Lexis Bane turned on the figure to help Draven down.

notes: The second half of Christmas Chaos. Its own last words report that the night's second main event could not be finished, there being no officials left in charge, and point the fed's most anticipated Heavyweight Championship crowning to the following Thursday.

name: Lord of the Asylum: Shock Syndrome

date.source: The fed's own newsdesk of 6 June 2002 reports two of this card's own finishes as having happened "this past week" — the three-way Women's title ladder finish and the Amira stand-off (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-05-to-06.html). The show itself carries no date of its own.

matches.note: Won by submission.
Won by pinfall, on Chris Kinsley's own DWO debut.

For the DWO Women's Championship. The fed's own results page scores it "Winner by ?: Kristi Kiss.. Lana Day.. Jaslene Myst..." and its own commentary says all three women appear to own the title; its newsdesk four days later reports Lana Day pinning Kristi Kiss for it, Jaslene Myst taking it off Lana Day, and Kristi Kiss winning it back with no pin. The outcome is left unresolved here because the fed itself left it unresolved.
Won by pinfall.

Judgment against Seth Valentine and Jonan, two on one, for the number one contendership to the DWO Extreme Championship — and, in the fed's own billing, “only one man can win” it. Recorded as a flat field with a single winner rather than as sides, because the stipulation makes the verdict individual: Jonan won by pinfall and left as the new contender, his own partner included in what he beat.
For the number one contendership to the DWO Tag Team Championship. The fed's own results page rules it "Winner of match six: No contest".

notes: The DWO's own pay-per-view, opened by a live Kittie set with the band's own singer named on-page and closed by a main event fought at the state hospital for a shot at the DWO Heavyweight Championship. The main event itself is not on the held page, which ends as the cameras leave for it; the fed's own card page (/promotions/dwo/archive/loa-shock-syndrome-card-2002.html) names its Final Six as Lethal, Switchblade, AJ Trinidad, Angelus, Gina Muniz and Amira. Northampton State Hospital is credited on-page as the show's sponsor.

name: Relentless, 25 September 2003

date.source: The page's own dateline, "September 25, 2003". The document's own <title> tag reads RelentlessAugust282003 — a stale template title carried forward, and not the date the page itself gives.

matches.note: The fed's own commentary calls Zahri a newcomer. The fed's own text names the referee "Mike Anderson" once mid-match, elsewhere simply "the ref"/"Ref".

notes: Opens with Zahri mistakenly attacking and injuring Rick Velocity backstage, thinking him her booked opponent; he is fired and Skorp takes the match, which Zahri wins by submission — the only bell-to-bell match the held page carries. A recap segment revisits an earlier, uncaptured Christian Darke/Stephanie Summers match (referee Tiddy O'Biddy) and stages a long Roulette/Gual backstage scene in which Roulette reveals a kayfabe backstory of Devil-cursed reincarnation and manifests a spirit, K.T. Two further matches are billed and then called off before either bell rings, both by Callisto Bane in person: Christian Darke (filling in for Stephanie Summers) vs. Gual, ruled "null and void"; and the advertised Intercontinental title three-way (Damian defending against Tyrone Grace and Sean Quinn), which Callisto interrupts to force Damian to vacate the Intercontinental title in exchange for a Heavyweight title shot against Donny Diamond at the coming pay-per-view, Descent into Darkness (dwo-descent-into-darkness-2003-09, collected: false) — Tyrone Grace and Sean Quinn are instead booked against each other there for both the vacant Intercontinental title and Sean Quinn's own Extreme Championship. Donny Diamond's own presence here, discussed as the reigning Heavyweight Champion and Damian's next opponent, is not reconciled anywhere held with Damian and Samantha's own claim five weeks earlier (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10) to have killed him — no document bridges the two, and neither is picked over the other. Also: Chryste is reported missing and possibly held for ransom; a stagehand delivers Jan Lilly's own ransom note to Callisto Bane, who is unmoved.

name: Thursday Night Travesty — the card, 13 June 2002

date.source: The card's own header: "Thursday Night Travesty 6.13.02 LIVE from Slaughter, Louisiana!" 13 June 2002 was a Thursday, the fed's own show night.

notes: An announced card, not a result: the page bills seven matches across low, middle and high card and names five further wrestlers under Other Appearences. No account of the show itself survives, so every appearance recorded here is a billing rather than a narrated performance. The page's own posting stamp reads "[ Datum ] 5-9-02" while the card it carries is for 13 June — the fed's own template carrying a stale date forward, the same shape this project's duplicate-filing discipline already names.

name: Thursday Night Travesty, 22 August 2002

date.source: The page's own posting stamp: "[ Datum ] 8-22-02". 22 August 2002 was a Thursday, the fed's own show night, and the capture is of the following day.

matches.note: The fed's own page rules it "Winner of Match One: Double Count out."
Mike Pizaz beat the reigning DWO World Champion by pinfall on his own debut, with the Circle of Rage at ringside; the title was not on the line.

notes: The show opens with the tag team Untitled — Drone and Ender — running The Fury out of the building and promising to take the Tag Team Championship off whoever holds it. The held page stops after the second match; the fed's own commentary announces AJ Trinidad's next title defence, against Jackson Rust at its own Blackshock.

name: Thursday Night Travesty — the main event, September 2002

date.source: CORRECTED on a 2026-08-29 cold re-read: the page's own closing line plugs an UPCOMING pay-per-view in the future tense — "don't forget, DWO is bringing to you Lord of the Asylum: UnStAbLe September 29, 2002!" — which places this show BEFORE 29 September 2002, not after it as the accession's original dating reasoned. The Wayback capture itself is dated 29 October 2002 (the page evidently sat unrefreshed on the server for weeks), which is what misled the original pass. Internal continuity narrows it further: Jackson Rust already holds the DWO World Title here, having apparently won it from AJ Trinidad at Blackshock (billed as upcoming on the fed's own Travesty of 22 August 2002, /promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2002-08-22.html), so this show falls between that Blackshock PPV and UnStAbLe — a September 2002 window, exact date not recoverable from the page itself.

matches.note: For the DWO World Title. Jackson Rust retained; Adam Stryker slapped him on the back afterwards and walked out.

notes: A main-event-only document — the fed served this match on its own page. Draven cuts in during it to say that after next week the belt will be around his waist.

name: Thursday Night Travesty, 22 May 2003

date.source: The fed's own filename dates the show to 22 May 2003, a Thursday, and the capture is of 8 June 2003. The page itself is headed a special edition of Travesty and carries no dateline of its own.

notes: A special edition of Travesty given over entirely to previewing the fed's own pay-per-view, Lord of the Asylum: Balls to the Wall — its commentary team works down that card match by match, cutting to camera-crew footage shot with the wrestlers between segments. Every appearance recorded here is a billing or a segment rather than a match on this show. The card it previews runs a four corners bondage match, a Rising Dominance title match for Carys, an Extreme title match for Chryste against Kuff McSlade, an Intercontinental defence against Kirk Morris, and a main event of Kaiowas against Kai Shinobi; none of its results is held.

name: Thursday Night Travesty, 10 July 2003

date.source: The page's own header — "Live from Reno, NV" — and the fed's own tour schedule, which announces "July 10, 2003 - Thursday Night Travesty will be visiting Reno, Nevada!" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-tour-dates-2003-07.html). 10 July 2003 was a Thursday.

matches.note: Billed as “Heaven and Hell” (Damian and Roulette). Roulette pinned Markus Stone with a phoenix splash while Damian held Ty Baron off; referee Kyra Stone. After the bell, The Real Deal turned on his own partner Ty Baron, hitting the Ten Ton Hammer off the top rope.
Komodo Dragon pinned Chainz after two consecutive Dragon Drops; referee Eddie Maneddi. Chainz was accompanied to the ring by his own valet, Tracy.

Billed Sean Quinn vs. Kaiowas, changed on-air to Sean Quinn vs. Angelus Sorrow. Quinn pinned Sorrow after a jawbreaker and a Rick Velocity super kick assist from ringside; referee Kara Stone. After the bell, Jade attacked both Rick Velocity and Angelus Sorrow.

Pola Bare (the fed's own spelling on this page) beat Regin with his own finisher, A Step Above, after a mist spray to the eyes. The first referee was knocked out mid-match and a second, unnamed referee finished the count.
A non-title match — the fed's own commentary calls Kaiowas the DWO World Champion while he loses it, and warns that next time the title will be on the line.
For the DWO Extreme Championship. Kuff McSlade retained the week after winning the belt; Tyrone Grace welcomed him into the DoD afterwards.

notes: All six matches are structured. Opens with a backstage scene in which Callisto Bane's own lawyer, Miranda Steel, clears Chryste of blame for her husband Kazuyin's own “accidental” death under his DWO contract's own liability clause, and Callisto sends her on a company-paid vacation. The main event closes with Damian and Samantha revealing on-air that they killed Donny Diamond at an LOA event the week before (see dwo-heavyweight-r006's own end and dwo-loa-donny-diamond-death-2003-07, collected: false), taking his pentagram necklace, and relaunching the Disciples of Darkness under Damian with Tyrone Grace, Sean Quinn, Komodo Dragon and Kuff McSlade as members.

notes: An announced card, not a result: the fed's own preview for its Travesty of 9 October 2003, written after a week off and billing five matches. Every appearance recorded here is a billing rather than a narrated performance — the results page it links to at the foot ("October 9, 2003 Results") was never captured. The card bills four debuts, three of them arrivals the page attributes to the collapse of Lights Out Wrestling: Jason Warrior, Reality/Mayhem and Michelle Raines. Seymour Almasy is billed against Christian Darke and Gaul of Fates Calling, the page saying he has spent two weeks sending the DWO messages about ending its reign of sin. The three arrivals billed from outside the DWO's own roster — Seymour Almasy, Jason Warrior and Reality/Mayhem — carry a kind: “billed” appearance each: the card billed them, which is the whole of what is claimed, and no held document says any of them worked the show. The results page the card links to was never captured and the DWO's own record stops the same week.

name: Lord of the Asylum — the event at which Donny Diamond was killed

date.source: The fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 has Damian and Samantha claim, on-air, to have killed Donny Diamond — Tyrone Grace's own words, “last week— the DWO World Champion — at LOA" (Samantha's own words: “what Damian and I did to Donny Diamond at LOA”), placing the event roughly a week before that broadcast (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

evidence.note: Tyrone Grace: “last week, my fucking mentor Donny Diamond was killed, by Damian—”; Samantha: “what Damian and I did to Donny Diamond at LOA— It was months before joining the DWO that Damian and I set our sights on Donny Diamond— ... And we saw the lives he ended— He was the perfect opportunity for us.” Damian is shown wearing what the text calls “the famous pentagram necklace of Donny Diamond,” taken as a trophy.

notes: No card or results page survives for this event. It ended the DWO World Heavyweight Championship reign of Donny Diamond (dwo-heavyweight-r006) by in-fiction death rather than a lost match, and is the occasion Damian gives for relaunching the Disciples of Darkness (disciples-of-darkness-dwo) the following week. Whether Kaiowas regained the vacant title at this same event or elsewhere is not stated anywhere held (dwo-heavyweight-r007).

name: Lord of the Asylum: Descent into Darkness

date.source: Relentless, 25 September 2003, calls it "a little over two days" away and, later the same page, "two days" away (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

evidence.note: Billed on-air as the DWO's own "end of the month pay-per-view event." Callisto Bane books Damian against Donny Diamond for the Heavyweight title, and Tyrone Grace against Sean Quinn for both the newly-vacated Intercontinental title and Sean Quinn's own Extreme Championship ("First and second pin get different titles").

notes: No card or results page survives. Damian's own participation, if it happened, would be his first billed appearance against Donny Diamond since Damian and Samantha's own claim (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10) to have killed him ten weeks earlier — unreconciled in anything held.
